location.name: Postpartum Unit — Texas Health Presbyterian Hospital Denton

text.paragraph: Postpartum care plan authored by Emily Carter, MD at 10/14/2026 6:53 PM following successful repeat VBAC. Mimi Shell is clinically stable immediately after delivery.

list.item: Routine postpartum monitoring of vital signs, uterine tone, lochia, and bleeding.
Routine oral analgesia as clinically indicated.
Perineal hygiene and comfort measures for first-degree laceration repair.
Encourage ambulation, hydration, and nutrition as appropriate.
Support breastfeeding, skin-to-skin, rooming-in, and lactation consultation if needed.
Assess postpartum mood, emotional well-being, home support, and safety.
Discuss reproductive goals and postpartum contraception options before discharge.
Return levothyroxine to pre-pregnancy dose of 100 mcg PO daily beginning the morning of October 15, 2026; reassess thyroid management with outpatient clinician.
Reinforce warning signs requiring urgent evaluation.
Transition longitudinal postpartum care back to Simone Heps at Health Services of North Texas.

tr.td: 2-week postpartum assessment: recovery, bleeding/pain, breastfeeding, mood, support, contraception, thyroid management, and interval concerns.

6-week comprehensive postpartum visit: physical recovery, chronic-condition follow-up, breastfeeding, mood screening, contraception/reproductive planning, preventive care, and transition to ongoing care.
Return to pre-pregnancy dose beginning the morning of October 15, 2026; outpatient thyroid reassessment planned.

text.paragraph: Plan: change from the pregnancy dose of 125 mcg daily to 100 mcg daily starting October 15; reassess thyroid function at approximately six weeks postpartum. This October 14 plan does not assert that future doses have already been administered.

Education should be reinforced during hospitalization and at discharge. Seek immediate evaluation for heavy bleeding, fever, severe or worsening headache, visual changes, chest pain, shortness of breath, severe abdominal pain, seizure, unilateral leg swelling or pain, or significant emotional or behavioral concerns.
